papers.title: Polarized training has greater impact on key endurance variables than threshold, high intensity, or high volume training
key_protocols: 80/20 intensity distribution (approx. 68% Zone 1 <LT1, 6% Zone 2 LT1-LT2, 26% Zone 3 >LT2)
Zone 1: <2 mmol/L blood lactate, Zone 2: 2-4 mmol/L, Zone 3: >4 mmol/L
Polarized training produced superior VO2max (+11.7%) and peak velocity/power (+5.1%) compared to threshold or high volume
papers.summary: Demonstrates that a 9-week polarized training intensity distribution yields significantly greater improvements in VO2max, time to exhaustion, and peak velocity compared to threshold, HIIT, or high-volume training in well-trained endurance athletes.

papers.title: Intervals, Thresholds, and Long Slow Distance: the Role of Intensity and Duration in Endurance Training
key_protocols: 3-Zone Physiological Model: Zone 1 (<VT1, <2.0 mM La, <80% HRmax), Zone 2 (VT1-VT2, 2.0-4.0 mM La, 82-88% HRmax), Zone 3 (>VT2, >4.0 mM La, >88-92% HRmax)
Session allocation rule: ~80% of sessions in Zone 1, <10% in Zone 2, 15-20% in Zone 3
Optimal interval prescription: 4 x 8 min @ 90-92% HRmax with 2 min active recovery
Autonomic recovery: Zone 1 restores HRV within <24h; Zone 2/3 suppresses HRV for 48-72h
papers.summary: Establishes the foundational 3-zone physiological framework and empirical evidence for 80/20 polarized training distribution and 4x8min interval dosing in endurance athletes.

papers.title: The Training Characteristics of World-Class Distance Runners: An Integration of Scientific Literature and Results-Proven Practice
key_protocols: Weekly volume norms: 130-190 km/week (5000m/10000m), 160-220 km/week (Marathon) over 11-14 sessions/week
Intensity distribution: >=80% low-intensity volume across annual cycle
Tapering protocol: 7-10 days exponential volume reduction (40-60% decrease) while maintaining frequency and interval intensity
Altitude training: 2000-2500m for 3-4 week blocks with 72h initial acclimatization buffer
papers.summary: Comprehensive synthesis of training characteristics, weekly volume benchmarks, periodization, tapering, and altitude strategies from 59 world-leading distance runners and Olympic coaches.

papers.title: Acute hamstring injuries in Swedish elite football: a prospective randomised controlled clinical trial comparing two rehabilitation protocols
key_protocols: L-Protocol 3-Exercise Suite: The Extender (3x12 twice daily), The Diver (3x6 every 3rd day), The Glider (3x4 every 3rd day)
Return to play significantly shortened: 28 days (L-Protocol) vs 51 days (Conventional Protocol)

RTP Clearance Criteria: Full active range of motion, zero palpation pain, maximum isometric strength parity >=95%, and Askling H-Test negative (0/10 pain and 0/10 insecurity during dynamic straight leg swing)
papers.summary: Randomized clinical trial demonstrating that lengthening exercises targeting eccentric contractions at elongated muscle lengths reduce return-to-play time by 45% and prevent hamstring re-injuries in elite football players.

papers.title: Acute hamstring injuries in Swedish elite sprinters and jumpers: a prospective randomised controlled clinical trial comparing two rehabilitation protocols
key_protocols: L-Protocol application in track and field sprinting/jumping athletes
RTP achieved in 49 days (L-Protocol) vs 86 days (Conventional Protocol)
Injury mechanism differentiation: High-speed sprinting injuries (biceps femoris) recover faster than stretch-type injuries (semimembranosus / proximal free tendon), which require extended remodeling
papers.summary: Validates the effectiveness of lengthening exercises in track and field sprinters and jumpers, demonstrating superior return-to-sport speed (49 vs 86 days) and establishing injury-type specific recovery trajectories.

papers.title: Continued sports activity, using a pain-monitoring model, during rehabilitation in patients with Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled study
papers.journal: The American Journal of Sports Medicine
key_protocols: VAS 0-10 Pain-Monitoring Decision Rules: 0-2 safe zone, 2-5 acceptable zone during/post activity, >5 unacceptable zone requiring immediate load reduction
24-Hour Recovery Rule: Pain and morning stiffness the day following tendon loading MUST return to pre-activity baseline
Continued sports loading under pain-monitoring model does NOT impair recovery compared to complete rest
papers.summary: Pioneering RCT establishing that continuing tendon loading under a structured pain-monitoring model (VAS <= 5 with 24h morning recovery) achieves equivalent clinical outcomes to rest while preserving athletic conditioning.

papers.title: A Proposed Return-to-Sport Program for Patients With Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy: Rationale and Implementation
papers.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy
key_protocols: Phase 1: Symptom Reduction & Low-Load Activation (Isometrics, double/single leg heel raises on flat ground)
Phase 2: Strength & Heavy Slow Resistance (Single-leg heel raises over ledge with added load, 3x15 progressing to 3x6-8 heavy)
Phase 3: Energy Storage & Plyometric Loading (Quick hops, skipping, jumping, eccentric-concentric stretch-shortening cycle)
Phase 4: Return to Full Sport / Trail Running (Sport-specific drills, hill running, uncontrolled terrain)
Minimum 12-week progression before high-speed competition clearance
papers.summary: Authoritative 4-phase clinical roadmap for midportion Achilles tendinopathy rehabilitation, integrating heavy slow resistance, progressive plyometric energy storage, and sport-specific clearance tests.

papers.title: Revisiting the continuum model of tendon pathology: what is its merit in clinical practice and research?
key_protocols: Tendon Continuum Tri-Phasic Model: Reactive Tendinopathy vs Tendon Disrepair vs Degenerative Tendinopathy
Reactive stage management: Deload fast energy storage/release, introduce heavy isometric holds (5 x 45s @ 70% MVC) for cortical analgesia and cell calming
Tendon disrepair / degenerative management: Progressive Heavy Slow Resistance (HSR) targeting collagen remodeling; load adjacent healthy tendon tissue
Avoid compressive loading at tendon insertion during reactive irritability
papers.summary: Refines the widely adopted Tendon Continuum Model, categorizing tendinopathy into reactive, disrepair, and degenerative stages with stage-matched exercise interventions (isometrics vs HSR vs energy storage).

papers.title: The training—injury prevention paradox: should athletes be training smarter and harder?
key_protocols: ACWR Mathematical Formula: Acute Workload (past 7 days) / Chronic Workload (past 28 days average)

Clinical Risk Zones: <0.8 (Under-training zone, elevated relative risk), 0.8-1.3 (The Sweet Spot, lowest injury risk <10%), 1.3-1.5 (Elevated risk / Caution zone), >1.5 (The Danger Zone, 2x to 4x injury risk spike)
Maximum safe weekly load expansion: <=10% to 15%
papers.summary: Establishes the Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio (ACWR) framework, showing that high chronic training loads build physical resilience while acute spikes (>1.5) exponentially increase soft-tissue injury risk.

papers.title: Neuromuscular Consequences of an Extreme Mountain Ultra-Marathon
key_protocols: Post-ultra neuromuscular deficits: Knee extensors MVC dropped by -35%, plantar flexors MVC dropped by -39%
Dual fatigue etiology: Central activation failure combined with excitation-contraction uncoupling from severe eccentric downhill muscle damage
Biological recovery window: 9 to 16 days required for voluntary force and blood biomarkers (CK, myoglobin) restoration
Mandatory 14-16 day post-ultra prohibition of downhill running, speedwork, and eccentric resistance loading
papers.summary: Investigates extreme mountain ultramarathon fatigue (166km, +9500m), quantifying central activation deficits and peripheral eccentric muscle damage, and defining the mandatory 9-16 day multi-stage recovery window.

papers.title: Effects of Strength Training on the Physiological Determinants of Middle- and Long-Distance Running Performance: A Systematic Review
key_protocols: Heavy resistance training (>=80% 1RM) or plyometric training 2-3 times per week for >=8 weeks
Improves Running Economy (RE) by 2% to 8% and enhances time-trial performance without muscle hypertrophy or VO2max penalty
Mechanisms: Enhanced musculotendinous stiffness, improved motor unit recruitment efficiency, and reduced metabolic cost of ground contact force
papers.summary: Definitive systematic review demonstrating that incorporating heavy resistance training or plyometrics 2-3x/week directly improves running economy by 2-8% and time-trial performance in distance runners without unwanted hypertrophy.
